newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia general rejects UN plea on child recruits.
newsitem.headline: Colombia general rejects UN plea on child recruits.

text.p: The commander-in-chief of the Colombian army accused a U.N. organisation of meddling on Saturday after it called for a ban on child recruits in the country's armed forces.

Gen. Manuel Jose Bonett, who said more than 4,000 minors between the ages of 15 and 18 serve in the Colombian army, said he had no intention of accepting the U.N. International Children's Emergency Fund's (UNICEF) recommendation to raise the minimum age of recruitment to 18.

"The government will continue to recruit minors into the ranks of the armed forces. These comments amount to meddling in the internal affairs of our country," Bonett said in an interview with the NTC-TV news programme.

In a report released last Wednesday in Bogota on the effects of armed conflict worldwide on children, UNICEF said: "Children in Colombia have suffered extreme violence in terms of deaths, injuries, abuse, torture, psychological trauma and recruitment into the armed forces and rebel groups."
Colombia's human rights ombudsman estimated about 2,500 children under age 18 were fighting in the ranks of the country's rebel armies.
A UNICEF spokeswoman said the organisation would not be deterred by Bonett's rejection of one of its central recommendations and would continue to press for its acceptance.
